question: Which word is an adjective describing the bright sun? ☀️
explanation: Awesome! 'Bright' is a describing word (adjective) that tells us how the sun looks in the positive degree! ☀️
hint: Look for the word that describes.

question: A turtle is slow, but a snail is even ___! 🐌
explanation: Great job! When comparing two animals (turtle and snail), we add '-er' to the adjective! 🐌

question: The cheetah is the ___ animal on land! 🐆
explanation: Super! When comparing more than two things, we add '-est' to make the superlative degree! 🚀
hint: Add '-est' for the number one spot.

question: The kitten has very ___ fur. 🐱
explanation: Fantastic! We use the positive degree 'soft' because we are just describing one kitten! 🧸
hint: Just one thing is being described.

question: An elephant is ___ than a lion. 🐘
explanation: Awesome! We double the 'g' and add '-er' when comparing two animals! 🐘

question: The giraffe is the ___ animal in the zoo. 🦒
explanation: Great job! The giraffe wins the top spot out of all animals, so we use '-est'! 🦒
hint: It is the number one highest.

question: This honey is very ___. 🍯
explanation: Super! We use the positive degree 'sweet' to describe just this one jar of honey! 🍯

question: Today is ___ than yesterday. ☀️
explanation: Fantastic! We are comparing two days, so we add '-er' to the word hot! ☀️

question: Antarctica is the ___ place on Earth! 🐧
explanation: Awesome! Out of all places on Earth, it is the number one, so we use '-est'! 🐧
hint: The most freezing place of all.

question: My school bag is very ___ today. 🎒
explanation: Great job! We are only talking about your bag, so we use the positive degree! 🎒

question: A feather is ___ than a rock. 🪶
explanation: Super! We compare a feather and a rock using the comparative '-er' word! 🪶

question: The Nile is the ___ river in the world. 🌊
explanation: Fantastic! It is the top river out of all rivers, so we use the superlative '-est'! 🌊

question: The baby looks very ___ playing with toys. 👶
explanation: Awesome! We just use 'happy' to describe the baby without comparing! 👶

question: I am ___ today than I was yesterday! 😊
explanation: Great job! We change the 'y' to 'i' and add '-er' to compare two days! 😊

question: Winning the game made him the ___ boy alive! 🥳
explanation: Super! For the number one level of happiness, we change 'y' to 'i' and add '-est'! 🥳

question: The butterfly is very ___. 🦋
explanation: Fantastic! 'Beautiful' is a long word, and here we use the positive degree for one butterfly! 🦋

question: A peacock is ___ than a pigeon. 🦚
explanation: Awesome! For long words like beautiful, we use 'more' to compare two things! 🦚

question: The sunset was the ___ sight of all! 🌅
explanation: Great job! For the number one spot with long words, we use 'most'! 🌅

question: Eating fruits is a ___ habit. 🍎
explanation: Super! 'Good' is the positive degree for this healthy habit! 🍎

question: Reading a book is ___ than watching TV. 📚
explanation: Fantastic! 'Good' changes to 'better' when we compare two things. It is a special irregular word! 📚

question: She is the ___ player on our whole team! 🏆
explanation: Awesome! 'Best' is the superlative form of good for the number one player! 🏆

question: Eating too much candy is a ___ idea. 🍬
explanation: Great job! 'Bad' is the positive degree for this tricky idea! 🍬
hint: The base word for negative things.

question: A toothache is ___ than a headache. 🦷
explanation: Super! 'Bad' changes to 'worse' when comparing two things. It is another special word! 🦷

question: That was the ___ storm of the year! 🌪️
explanation: Fantastic! 'Worst' is the superlative degree of bad for the number one biggest storm! 🌪️

question: A mouse is ___ than a cat. 🐁
explanation: Awesome! We add '-er' to compare the size of the mouse and the cat! 🐁

question: An ant is the ___ insect here. 🐜
explanation: Great job! Out of all insects, the ant takes the '-est' for being the tiniest! 🐜

question: A tiger is ___ than a fox. 🐅
explanation: Super! We use '-er' to compare the strength of a tiger and a fox! 🐅

question: The elephant is the ___ animal in the jungle! 🐘
explanation: Fantastic! The elephant gets the '-est' because it is number one in strength! 🐘

question: The clown at the circus is very ___. 🤡
explanation: Awesome! We are just describing the clown, so we use the positive word 'funny'! 🤡

question: This joke is ___ than the last one! 😂
explanation: Great job! Change the 'y' to 'i' and add '-er' to compare two jokes! 😂

question: That is the ___ movie I have ever seen! 🤣
explanation: Super! For the absolute best laugh out of all movies, we use the superlative '-est'! 🤣

question: A blanket is ___ than a sheet. 🛌
explanation: Fantastic! We compare the blanket and the sheet by adding '-er'! 🛌

question: This is the ___ winter coat in the store! 🧥
explanation: Awesome! Out of all the coats, this one wins the '-est' for being the most warm and thick! 🧥
hint: Number one out of all coats.

question: A piece of paper is ___ than a book. 📄
explanation: Great job! We double the 'n' and add '-er' to compare paper and a book! 📄

question: This thread is the ___ string in the box! 🧵
explanation: Super! Out of all strings, it takes the '-est' for being the finest one! 🧵

question: A pencil is ___ than a computer. ✏️
explanation: Fantastic! We add '-er' to compare the price of a pencil and a computer! ✏️

question: This is the ___ toy in the whole shop! 🧸
explanation: Awesome! It is the number one lowest price of all, so we use '-est'! 🧸

question: The sky is ___ at night than in the morning. 🌃
explanation: Great job! We add '-er' to compare night and morning skies! 🌃

question: Midnight is the ___ time of the day. 🌌
explanation: Super! Midnight wins the top spot for darkness, so we use '-est'! 🌌

question: My room is ___ than my brother's room! 🧹
explanation: Fantastic! We add '-er' to compare your room and your brother's room! 🧹

question: Our classroom is the ___ room in the school! ✨
explanation: Awesome! Out of all rooms, ours is the number one, so we add '-est'! ✨

question: An apple is ___ than a lemon. 🍎
explanation: Great job! We compare the apple and the lemon by adding '-er' to sweet! 🍎

question: This chocolate is the ___ candy of all! 🍫
explanation: Super! Out of all candies, chocolate wins the '-est' for being the most sweet! 🍫

question: The swimming pool is ___ than the bathtub. 🏊
explanation: Fantastic! We compare the pool and the tub using the '-er' ending! 🏊

question: The ocean is the ___ body of water on Earth. 🌊
explanation: Awesome! The ocean is the ultimate number one, so we use the superlative '-est'! 🌊

question: A lion's roar is ___ than a dog's bark. 🦁
explanation: Great job! We add '-er' to compare the sound of the lion and the dog! 🦁

question: Thunder makes the ___ sound in a storm! 🌩️
explanation: Super! Out of all sounds, thunder is number one, so we use '-est'! 🌩️

question: A sponge is ___ than a piece of wood. 🧽
explanation: Fantastic! We compare the sponge and wood by adding '-er' to soft! 🧽

question: This cloud looks like the ___ pillow in the sky! ☁️
explanation: Awesome! Out of all clouds, it gets the '-est' for looking the most fluffy! ☁️

question: My grandfather is ___ than my father. 👴
explanation: Great job! We use '-er' to compare the ages of two people! 👴
